# Independent interoperability fixtures

The synthetic fixture data in this directory is dedicated to the public domain under **CC0-1.0**. It contains no customer workbooks. The repository's code remains under its existing license.

`basic.fods` is hand-authored Flat ODF, not generated by OpenSheet or SheetJS. `manifest.json` indexes the covered features, expected scalar results, known losses and independent-reader procedure. The generated evidence preserves source FODS plus LibreOffice-authored XLSX, OpenSheet-exported XLSX and LibreOffice-reopened XLSX with SHA-256 hashes. The automated fixture tests consume those saved files; they do not require LibreOffice in CI.

The current reader is LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0. This is an alpha build, not evidence for all stable LibreOffice releases or Excel. Its boolean-to-formula rewrite is recorded as a difference, not hidden by converting `1` back to `true`. LibreOffice documents TYPE result `8` as a formula in its [information functions reference](https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-GB/text/scalc/01/04060104.html). Consequently the TYPE probe distinguishes the changed cell representation, rather than establishing a different logical result.

The separately indexed openpyxl rule fixture verifies disclosure of three validation rules and two conditional-formatting ranges when raw worksheet parts are present; the rules themselves are not imported. Without raw parts those losses cannot be detected by this scan. Stylesheets/font rendering, exact column widths, images/charts/macros, rule preservation and visual review are not established by these fixtures. Further feature-indexed fixtures are still required before IO-01/IO-03 can close.

Each manifest entry records a SHA-256 of its `source` file and links existing evidence, provenance, expected loss and an independent-reader procedure. A source can be a fixture file or a generator script: hashing a generator does not authenticate a subsequently generated workbook. Some ZIP writers include timestamps, so regeneration can produce different bytes even when independent readback agrees.

Two openpyxl 3.1.5 fixtures cover global and sheet-scoped defined names, with and without formulas referencing them. Import reports three lost names; the formula fixture reports two affected formulas and retains their expressions. Strict import rejects those losses. For SheetJS parsing before adapter conversion, `sheetStubs: true` is required in this fixture to retain formulas without cached values. The tests do not establish Excel compatibility or independent calculation of those formulas.

Two independently authored openpyxl fixtures cover the 1900 and 1904 date systems, a leap-day time, a 2100 date and a date arithmetic formula. The manifest records actual XLSX serials and the dropped default margins; openpyxl does not calculate formulas. The generated report separately records in-memory serials because the writer rounds the fractional value by one floating-point step in the stored XML. The fictitious 1900 leap day, zero serial and Excel behavior are not covered by these fixtures.

LibreOfficeDev subsequently recalculated both uncached source files and OpenSheet exports; the retained [round-trip evidence](../../../benchmarks/date-system-reader-verified-2026-11-22.json) records rewritten format codes and a small numerical serialization difference. The source generator alone does not calculate the formulas.
